findings.title: Embedded-post username colour has its light/dark lightness values swapped
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). A correct dark-theme conversion must keep 30% for the light branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for the dark branch, but this line uses 70% for $primary and 30% for $secondary. Light-theme embedded-post usernames therefore become far paler than before and the dark-theme colour is far darker than intended, reducing readability in both themes.

findings.title: Group-member name colour changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This line converts it to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% on $secondary for dark. The light-theme name colour is therefore changed unnecessarily and the dark-theme colour is darker than the intended equivalent, weakening contrast.

findings.title: Custom-message-length colour has its light/dark lightness values swapped
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). A correct conversion must keep 70% for the light branch and use scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) for the dark branch, matching the equivalent desktop/modal.scss rule, but this line uses 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary. Both themes therefore get the opposite shade from the one intended for the character-count hint.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading colour changes the original 20% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The original mobile rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), and the equivalent desktop topic-map heading correctly converts to 20% on $primary with 80% on $secondary for dark. This line instead uses 50% for both branches. Mobile topic-map headings become much paler in the light theme and much darker than intended in the dark theme, losing heading contrast.

findings.title: Mobile group-member name colour changes the original 30% lightness to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). This line converts it to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% on $secondary for dark. The light-theme name colour is therefore changed unnecessarily and the dark-theme colour is darker than the intended equivalent, weakening contrast.
